claim.claim-text: A closed-loop atmospheric terraforming spire (1600) comprising: an intake blower (1602) ingesting ambient planetary atmosphere; a plurality of Cool Power Core modules (1604) each including a 90°C CVD-graphene hydrodynamic vortex cavitator (104), a 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching nanosecond pulsed plasma stage (106), and an 8YSZ oxygen-ion membrane (108); a thermal radiator fin array (1606) coupled to a cryogenic planetary ambient cold sink; and a solid-carbon and nitrate synthesis reactor (1608) converting dissociated carbon dioxide and nitrogen into structural carbon allotropes, breathable oxygen, and fixed agricultural fertilizer.

The closed-loop atmospheric terraforming spire (1600) of claim 44, wherein the planetary atmosphere comprises Martian carbon dioxide at 500 to 800 Pa and -60°C, and wherein the spire exports at least 340 kWe per 1,000 cores while producing solid graphitic carbon and ammonium nitrate.

The closed-loop atmospheric terraforming spire (1600) of claim 44, further comprising a regolith perchlorate wash loop (1610) decomposing ClO4- ions in the 33.6 kV nanosecond plasma stage (106) into benign chloride salts and gaseous oxygen.

A sub-glacial cryo-volcanic melt and abyssal exploration rover (1700) comprising: a radiation-hardened chassis (1702) rated to 10^8 Gy; a plurality of Cool Power Core units (1704) incorporating 4H-SiC betavoltaic liners (402); an acoustic-cavitation plasma ice-fracturing nosecone (1706) driven by a 33.6 kV pulsed exciter (106); and a closed-loop heat-pipe condenser (1708) rejecting heat to surrounding cryogenic ice or abyssal ocean water to generate continuous propulsion and sensor power.

The sub-glacial cryo-volcanic melt and abyssal exploration rover (1700) of claim 47, wherein the acoustic-cavitation plasma nosecone (1706) induces micro-spallation in 95 K cryogenic ice to reduce thermal melt enthalpy requirements by at least 35 percent.

The sub-glacial cryo-volcanic melt and abyssal exploration rover (1700) of claim 47, further comprising a seafloor hydrothermal plume intake (1710) harvesting 140°C vent fluid against 2°C abyssal seawater across thermoelectric arrays (112) to sustain multi-year autonomous seafloor operation.

An intercity evacuated pneumatic-maglev transit system (1800) comprising: a low-pressure guideway tube (1802); a vacuum roughing-pump station (1804) maintaining sub-atmospheric tube pressure; a Cool Power Core thermal-harvesting array (1806) thermally coupled to heat exchangers on the vacuum roughing-pump station (1804) and linear-motor stators (1808) as a 90°C to 95°C hot-side input; and a sub-surface geothermal or marine cold-sink loop (1810) coupled to thermoelectric generators (112) to export net continuous electricity to the guideway.

The intercity evacuated pneumatic-maglev transit system (1800) of claim 50, further comprising a high-speed rail dynamic-braking resistor heat exchanger (1812) transferring regenerative braking thermal pulses into a 90°C thermal buffer tank (102).

The intercity evacuated pneumatic-maglev transit system (1800) of claim 50, wherein each passenger transit pod (1814) incorporates an onboard closed-loop life-support core (1816) recycling cabin condensate, carbon dioxide, and lavatory wastewater via 90°C graphene cavitation and 33.6 kV plasma without external sewage discharge.

A submerged transoceanic maglev conduit (1900) comprising: a positively buoyant double-walled composite pressure hull (1902) suspended 150 to 300 meters below sea level; tension-leg seafloor tethers (1904) anchored by suction caissons (1906) with 6-DOF seismic gimbals (1908); and a distributed Cool Power Core array (1910) bridging internal vacuum-pump and eddy-current heat against 2°C ambient seawater while limiting external thermal plume elevation to less than 0.1 K at 1.0 meter radial distance.

The submerged transoceanic maglev conduit (1900) of claim 53, further comprising a continental-shelf methane-seep capture hood (1912) routing natural seafloor methane bubbles into the 33.6 kV plasma stage (106) for conversion into solid carbon and hydrogen.

The submerged transoceanic maglev conduit (1900) of claim 53, wherein the conduit terminates at a semi-submersible floating ocean sanctuary hub (1914) integrating zero-brine seawater desalination, mineral extraction, and a climate-controlled geodesic habitat.
